title: perf: establish 3000-node performance baseline and test harness
description: Establish a measurable performance baseline for the application using 3000 nodes, profiling rendering, pan/zoom, and selection operations.

ubiquitous: THE SYSTEM SHALL collect and store performance metrics for 3000-node documents

event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL log the load latency and initialization time

unwanted.condition: IF the benchmark test fails to complete
unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT crash silently
unwanted.because: we need partial telemetry to debug performance bottlenecks

preconditions: Test document with 3000 nodes is generated
invariants: Metric collection does not alter the document state

happy: PERF-001 runs successfully on 3000 nodes and outputs rendering FPS
PERF-002 captures zoom/pan frame rates correctly under sustained interaction
error: Metrics fallback if frame tracking API fails to initialize
Memory exhaustion handles gracefully without corrupting document state

questions: How do we measure accurate FPS in headless Dioxus tests?

phase_0: Research headless performance measurement in Dioxus
phase_2: Implement PERF-001 and PERF-002 measurement harness

title: perf: implement viewport virtualization and LOD for large documents
description: Implement viewport-based virtualization and Level of Detail (LOD) simplification to guarantee 120 FPS on 3000-node documents.

ubiquitous: THE SYSTEM SHALL maintain 120 FPS during all interactions with 3000 nodes

event_driven.trigger: WHEN a node moves outside the viewport bounds
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL omit the node from the rendering tree

unwanted.condition: IF a node is partially inside the viewport
unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT omit the node from the rendering tree
unwanted.because: clipping must be handled visually, not skipped entirely

preconditions: Viewport bounds are known and updated on pan/zoom
postconditions: Only visible nodes and edges are rendered
invariants: Virtualization does not affect selection state

happy: Nodes fully outside viewport are not rendered in DOM
Edges connecting to off-screen nodes are still rendered if they cross viewport bounds
error: Degraded mode when spatial index update fails falls back to naive rendering
Handling extreme zoom levels gracefully without float precision crashes

questions: What is the most efficient spatial index for Dioxus web/desktop?

phase_2: Filter render list based on viewport intersection

title: subgraphs: implement SUB-* reliability and reparenting logic
description: Fix and complete the subgraph grouping, parent-child relationships, and container boundary logic based on SUB-* test cases.

ubiquitous: THE SYSTEM SHALL prevent circular parent-child relationships

event_driven.trigger: WHEN a child node is dragged outside its parent container bounds
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL auto-expand the parent container to enclose the child

unwanted.condition: IF a parent subgraph is deleted
unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT implicitly delete its children
unwanted.because: children must be reparented to the root layer to avoid unintended data loss

preconditions: Node target is of kind Subgraph
postconditions: Child node parent_id points to the target Subgraph
invariants: No node can be its own ancestor

happy: Moving a child updates its relative position, keeping it in the parent
Deleting a parent moves children to the root layer
error: Attempting to set a node's parent to itself returns CircularParent error
Attempting to reparent to a non-subgraph node returns InvalidParent error

questions: How do we handle multi-select dragging of parent and child simultaneously?

phase_0: Implement cycle detection in schema validation
phase_1: Implement reparenting logic to adjust absolute to relative coords
phase_2: Write and pass SUB-001 to SUB-034 test suite
